title: Charged for seats that were removed
context: Workspace WS-2210 on a per-seat plan at 14.00 per user. Four users were removed on the 3rd; the invoice on the 5th still bills 22 seats. Seat reductions apply at the next renewal under the plan terms. The agent can issue a prorated credit as goodwill.
customer_turns: Workspace WS-2210 was invoiced for twenty-two seats on the fifth, but I removed four people on the third. We are paying for users who no longer have accounts.
I removed them through the admin console and the user list shows eighteen today. Nobody told me reductions only take effect at renewal.
Credit us for the four seats for this period, or explain why not. I need an answer I can take to our finance team.
resolution_space: Issue a prorated credit for the four seats
Explain the renewal-boundary rule and uphold the invoice
Apply the reduction immediately and credit from today
Escalate to the billing team

title: Annual plan charged at the monthly rate
context: Account AC-77120 switched to an annual plan at 1,320.00 on the 12th. The invoice on the 14th charges 132.00 monthly instead; the annual discount of 20 percent was not applied. The agent can reissue the invoice on the annual rate.
customer_turns: I switched account AC-77120 to the annual plan on the twelfth, and the invoice I received on the fourteenth charges the monthly rate.
I chose annual specifically for the twenty percent discount, and the confirmation screen clearly showed the annual total before I paid anything at all.
Reissue the invoice on the annual terms and tell me what I owe. Our finance system needs a single correct document for the year.
resolution_space: Reissue the invoice on the annual rate with the discount applied
Credit the difference against the next invoice
Revert to monthly billing and refund the switch
Escalate to the billing team

title: Overage charge for API calls above the included quota
context: Project PR-5518, plan includes 500,000 API calls per month; 812,000 were recorded, producing an overage of 156.00. A retry loop in the customer's integration generated roughly 300,000 duplicate calls. The agent can waive one overage per account per year.
customer_turns: Project PR-5518 has a hundred and fifty-six pound overage charge on it for API calls. We have never gone over the included quota before.
We found a retry loop in our integration that repeated the same request for about two days. It was our bug, but nothing useful came of those calls.
We have fixed it on our side. Is there any relief available for a first occurrence like this, and what would it take?
resolution_space: Waive the overage under the annual first-occurrence allowance
Charge the overage and enable a usage alert
Apply a partial credit for the duplicate calls
Escalate to the billing team

title: Tax applied despite a registered exemption
context: Organisation OR-3390 supplied a valid tax registration number twelve days ago; it is stored but not marked validated, so tax of 64.00 was charged on the last invoice. The agent can validate the number and credit the tax charged since the submission date.
customer_turns: Organisation OR-3390 has been charged sixty-four pounds of tax on the latest invoice, even though we gave you our registration number twelve days ago.
The number is showing in the billing settings, so it reached you. It just does not seem to be doing anything to the invoices.
Validate it and credit the tax on the invoice that has already been issued. Confirm future invoices will be clean from now on.
resolution_space: Validate the number and credit the tax charged
Validate the number for future invoices only
Request supporting documentation before validating
Escalate to the tax compliance team

title: Trial converted to a paid plan without notice
context: Account AC-91002, 30-day trial ended on the 9th and converted to a 89.00 monthly plan. Trial reminder emails were sent to the signup address, which bounced. The product was not used during the trial. The agent can refund the first period and cancel.
customer_turns: Account AC-91002 was charged eighty-nine pounds when our trial ended. I did not know the trial was even close to expiring at all.
Nobody on the team logged in after the first week, so we got no value from it at all. The signup address was a colleague who has since left.
Refund the charge and cancel the plan. If you cannot refund it, say so now rather than after I have waited a week.
resolution_space: Refund the first period and cancel the plan
Cancel the plan without a refund
Convert the charge to account credit
Escalate to the billing team

title: Price increase applied mid-term
context: Contract CT-4408, a twelve-month term at a fixed rate signed in March. A platform price rise was applied from September, adding 47.00 per month. The contract fixes the rate for the term. The agent can restore the contracted rate and credit the difference.
customer_turns: Our invoice under contract CT-4408 has gone up by forty-seven pounds a month since September. We signed a twelve-month fixed rate in March.
The contract we hold states the rate is fixed for the term, and we have six months of it left to run. Nobody contacted us about a change.
Put the price back to the contracted rate and credit what we have overpaid since September. Confirm both of those before we finish.
resolution_space: Restore the contracted rate and credit the overcharge
Apply the contracted rate going forward only
Review the contract terms before adjusting
Escalate to the contracts team

title: Data export still pending after three days
context: Export job EX-66104 requested three days ago over a 90 GB workspace. Large exports are queued and the published estimate is 24 hours. The job is stalled behind a queue backlog. The agent can requeue at high priority or split the export by project.
customer_turns: Export job EX-66104 has been sitting pending for three days now. Your published documentation says large exports usually complete within twenty-four hours.
We need the archive for an audit that starts on Thursday, and the workspace is around ninety gigabytes across eleven projects in total.
Either get it moving or give me another way to obtain the data by Thursday. Tell me which of those you can actually do today.
resolution_space: Requeue the export at high priority with a stated completion time
Split the export into per-project jobs
Provide direct API access for the customer to pull the data
Escalate to the platform operations team

title: Support ticket past the contracted response time
context: Ticket SD-91188, priority high, opened 31 hours ago. The contracted first-response time at this plan tier is 8 hours. The ticket was auto-routed to an inactive queue. The agent can reassign it to an on-duty engineer immediately.
customer_turns: Ticket SD-91188 was raised as high priority thirty-one hours ago and nobody has responded. Our contract says eight hours for a first response.
It concerns failed webhook deliveries that are affecting our order processing, so it is not something we can leave sitting over the weekend.
Get an engineer onto it now and tell me who owns it by name. I also want the response-time breach formally recorded against our account.
resolution_space: Reassign the ticket to an on-duty engineer immediately
Record the response-time breach and apply any service credit
Schedule a call with the assigned engineer
Escalate to the support operations manager

title: Requested feature flag not enabled
context: Workspace WS-4471 requested the beta audit-log feature nineteen days ago. Beta enablement requires a signed beta agreement, which was never sent to the customer. The agent can send the agreement and enable within one working day of signature.
customer_turns: We asked for the audit log beta on workspace WS-4471 nineteen days ago and it is still not enabled. The request shows as received.
Our security review needs the audit log before we can roll the product out to the wider team next month, and that date is fixed.
Tell me what is still outstanding and enable it. If something is needed from us, send it over to me today, not next week.
resolution_space: Send the beta agreement and enable on signature
Enable the feature under the existing master agreement
Provide an interim log export in place of the feature
Escalate to the product team

title: Account migration to a new region not completed
context: Migration request MG-22087 to the European data region, submitted five weeks ago; the published window is fifteen working days. The migration is paused pending the customer's confirmation of a maintenance window, which was never requested. The agent can book the window.
customer_turns: Our migration to the European region under MG-22087 was submitted five weeks ago. Your published window is fifteen working days and nothing has moved.
Our data protection officer is asking for a completion date for a compliance report due at the end of the month, which we cannot move.
Tell me what is holding it and give me a date. If you need something from us, ask for it now rather than later.
resolution_space: Book the maintenance window and commit to a migration date
Provide a written status letter for the compliance report
Expedite the migration to the next available slot
Escalate to the migrations team

title: Refund approved but not paid
context: Refund RF-30055 for 640.00 approved twenty-two days ago; the stated payout time is ten working days. The payout failed because the bank details on file belong to a closed account. No failure notice was sent. The agent can collect new details and reissue.
customer_turns: Refund RF-30055 for six hundred and forty pounds was approved twenty-two days ago. Your team said ten working days and nothing has arrived.
We have checked with our bank and nothing has come in. The account we originally paid from was closed when we changed banks in the summer.
Take our current bank details and reissue it today. Tell me when the money will actually be with us, to the day.
resolution_space: Collect new bank details and reissue the payout
Apply the amount as account credit instead
Verify the failed payout record before reissuing
Escalate to the finance team

title: Security questionnaire response overdue
context: Request SQ-11290 for a completed vendor security questionnaire, submitted seventeen days ago; the stated turnaround is ten working days. The questionnaire sits with the security team awaiting review. The agent can share the current compliance pack immediately.
customer_turns: We sent a security questionnaire under SQ-11290 seventeen days ago and have had no response at all. Your site says ten working days.
Our procurement team cannot approve the renewal without it, and the current term ends in three weeks. They will not sign on a promise.
Get me the completed questionnaire this week, and send whatever compliance documents you can share right now so procurement has something in the meantime.
resolution_space: Share the current compliance pack immediately and chase the questionnaire
Commit to a completion date with the security team
Arrange a call between the security teams
Escalate to the security compliance team

title: Webhooks failing with timeout errors
context: Workspace WS-8802. Webhook deliveries to the customer's endpoint fail with timeouts; the endpoint responds in about 9 seconds against a 5-second delivery timeout. Failed events are retained for 72 hours. The agent can replay events and cannot raise the timeout.
customer_turns: Webhooks on workspace WS-8802 have been failing since Monday with timeout errors. We are missing customer order events as a result of that.
Our endpoint did get slower after a release last week, but it still returns a successful response eventually, usually within about nine seconds.
Replay everything we have missed since Monday, and tell me what response time we need to hit so this stops happening again next week.
resolution_space: Replay the failed events within the retention window
Explain the delivery timeout and required response time
Enable queued delivery with backoff for the endpoint
Escalate to the platform engineering team

title: Single sign-on login loop
context: Organisation OR-6640 using SAML single sign-on. Users are returned to the login page after authenticating; the identity provider's signing certificate was rotated two days ago and the stored certificate is stale. The agent can update the certificate and can enable a temporary bypass for admins.
customer_turns: Nobody in organisation OR-6640 can sign in. We authenticate with our identity provider and get sent straight back to your login page.
Our identity team rotated a signing certificate two days ago as part of a scheduled renewal. That is the only change we know of.
Fix the login and get at least our admins back in today. Forty people cannot do any work at all until this is resolved.
resolution_space: Update the stored signing certificate and restore sign-on
Enable temporary password login for administrators
Disable single sign-on enforcement until the certificate is fixed
Escalate to the identity engineering team

title: Reports show stale data
context: Workspace WS-1193. Dashboard figures are 36 hours behind live records because the nightly aggregation job has failed for two consecutive nights on a schema change. The agent can trigger a manual rebuild and can provide a live query export.
customer_turns: The reports in workspace WS-1193 are showing numbers that are a day and a half out of date. The underlying records are correct.
We noticed because yesterday's sales do not appear at all, while everything older than Tuesday looks right. It is consistent across every dashboard.
Rebuild the data and get me an accurate figure for yesterday before lunchtime. Our board meeting is at four and I present these numbers.
resolution_space: Trigger a manual aggregation rebuild with a stated completion time
Provide a live query export for the missing period
Confirm the failure and register an incident
Escalate to the data platform team

title: File uploads failing above a size threshold
context: Workspace WS-7729 on a plan with a 100 MB per-file upload limit. Uploads between 100 MB and 400 MB fail with a generic error rather than a size message. The agent can explain the limit, enable chunked upload, and cannot raise the limit on this plan.
customer_turns: Uploads in workspace WS-7729 fail for our larger files. The error just says upload failed with no explanation of what went wrong.
Small files go through fine. The ones failing are video files between about a hundred and four hundred megabytes, which we need to share with clients.
Tell me what the actual limit is and how we work with files this size. A plain answer is more useful than another retry.
resolution_space: Explain the per-file limit and enable chunked upload
Recommend a plan whose limit covers the file sizes
Provide a direct storage link for the large files
Escalate to the platform engineering team

title: Integration disconnects every few hours
context: Workspace WS-3345 connected to a third-party calendar service. The connection drops roughly every four hours because the refresh token is being invalidated by a conflicting second connection from the same account. The agent can remove the duplicate connection and reauthorise.
customer_turns: Our calendar integration on workspace WS-3345 disconnects every few hours. We reconnect it and it drops again by the afternoon the same day.
Someone on the team may have connected the same calendar account a second time when they were setting up their own view last month.
Find the conflict and leave us with one working connection that stays up. I do not want to be reconnecting this every single day.
resolution_space: Remove the duplicate connection and reauthorise once
Reset all integration tokens and reconnect
Advise the customer to revoke access at the calendar provider
Escalate to the integrations team

title: Search returns no results for recent documents
context: Workspace WS-5507. Documents created in the last nine days are missing from search because the indexing worker for that shard is backlogged. Older documents are searchable. The agent can trigger a reindex and can provide a direct listing view.
customer_turns: Search in workspace WS-5507 is not finding anything created in the last week or so. Older documents still come up immediately as they always did.
The documents are definitely there, because we can open them from the folder listing. It is only search that cannot see them at all.
Reindex whatever needs reindexing and tell me when search will be complete again. We rely on it heavily here every single day.
resolution_space: Trigger a reindex of the affected shard with a stated completion time
Provide a filtered listing view for the missing period
Confirm the backlog and register an incident
Escalate to the search platform team

title: Cancelling an annual plan after two months
context: Account AC-2214 on an annual plan of 2,400.00 paid in advance, two months used. The terms are non-refundable mid-term but allow cancellation at renewal. The agent can offer a downgrade or a credit and cannot refund the remaining ten months.
customer_turns: We want to cancel the annual plan on account AC-2214. We paid two thousand four hundred pounds up front and have used two months of it.
Our team has shrunk and we no longer need the product at this scale. Our finance director is asking about the unused ten months.
Tell me plainly what we can recover. If nothing at all, tell me what else you can offer instead of a refund.
resolution_space: Explain the non-refundable term and set the renewal to cancel
Offer a downgrade for the remaining term
Issue account credit for the unused months
Escalate to the accounts team

title: Refund for a duplicate subscription
context: Two subscriptions, SB-7701 and SB-7703, both active for the same organisation at 199.00 monthly; the second was created during a failed checkout retry and has never had users assigned. The agent can cancel the unused subscription and refund three months.
customer_turns: We are being billed twice, on subscriptions SB-7701 and SB-7703, at a hundred and ninety-nine pounds each for the same organisation every month.
Only one of them has any users on it. The other was probably created when the checkout page errored and I submitted it again.
Cancel the empty one and refund what we have paid on it. Tell me exactly how many months you are returning to us.
resolution_space: Cancel the unused subscription and refund three months
Cancel the unused subscription with a credit instead of a refund
Merge the subscriptions and adjust the next invoice
Escalate to the billing team

title: Downgrading before renewal
context: Workspace WS-9910 on the Business tier at 45.00 per user, renewing in six days with 40 users. The Standard tier at 22.00 lacks the audit log and advanced permissions. The agent can schedule the downgrade at renewal and cannot downgrade mid-term.
customer_turns: Workspace WS-9910 renews in six days on the Business tier at forty-five pounds a user. With forty users that is more than we can justify.
We use almost none of the advanced features. The one thing we would miss is granular permissions, which I understand is not in Standard.
Move us to Standard at renewal. Tell me what we lose the day it changes so I can warn the team in advance.
resolution_space: Schedule the downgrade at renewal and list the features lost
Apply a discount to retain the current tier
Reduce seat count instead of downgrading tier
Escalate to the accounts team

title: Refund after an extended outage
context: Organisation OR-5590 experienced 14 hours of unavailability last month. The service agreement credits 10 percent of the monthly fee for outages between 8 and 24 hours; the monthly fee is 1,100.00. The agent can apply the contractual credit.
customer_turns: Organisation OR-5590 lost fourteen hours of service last month. We could not process anything at all for most of an entire working day.
Our contract has service credits in it, though I do not have the exact percentages to hand. Our monthly fee is eleven hundred pounds.
Apply whatever credit we are owed and tell me the exact figure. If we are owed nothing at all, explain to me why.
resolution_space: Apply the contractual 10 percent service credit
Apply a larger goodwill credit given the business impact
Provide the outage report and confirm the credit calculation
Escalate to the account management team

title: Cancelling an add-on purchased in error
context: Workspace WS-6118 purchased an advanced analytics add-on at 300.00 annually four days ago. The add-on has never been opened. The 14-day cancellation window applies to add-ons. The agent can cancel and refund in full.
customer_turns: We bought the advanced analytics add-on on workspace WS-6118 four days ago for three hundred pounds and nobody has even opened it once.
It was purchased by a team lead who did not realise the reporting we needed is already included in our plan at no extra cost.
Cancel it and refund the three hundred pounds. Confirm whether it counts against anything else on the account before you do it.
resolution_space: Cancel the add-on and refund in full within the window
Cancel with a prorated refund
Convert the add-on value to account credit
Escalate to the billing team

title: Auto-renewal after a written cancellation notice
context: Contract CT-8823 renewed for twelve months at 5,400.00. A cancellation notice was sent by email to the account manager 45 days before renewal; the contract requires notice through the billing portal. The agent can honour the notice as a contract remedy.
customer_turns: Contract CT-8823 has auto-renewed for another year at five thousand four hundred pounds, and we gave notice in writing forty-five days before renewal.
We sent it by email to our account manager, who acknowledged it. I understand the contract names the billing portal, but the notice was clearly given.
Reverse the renewal and cancel the contract as we asked. I can forward you the whole email chain today if you need it.
resolution_space: Honour the emailed notice and reverse the renewal
Uphold the renewal under the portal notice requirement
Shorten the renewed term as a compromise
Escalate to the contracts team

title: Sole administrator has left the company
context: Workspace WS-4402. The only administrator account belongs to a departed employee whose mailbox is closed. Admin transfer requires verification of domain ownership plus a request from a verified billing contact. The agent can start the transfer process.
customer_turns: The only administrator on workspace WS-4402 left the company last month and we cannot add or remove anyone. Her mailbox is closed.
I am the finance contact and I pay the invoices, but my account is a standard member with no admin rights at all on the workspace.
Transfer administration to me. Tell me exactly what proof you need, where to send it, and how long the whole thing takes.
resolution_space: Start the admin transfer with domain ownership verification
Require a written request on company letterhead
Grant temporary elevated access pending verification
Escalate to the account security team

title: Two-factor device lost
context: User account ending 3320 with app-based two-factor authentication. The device is lost and no recovery codes were saved. Reset requires verification by an organisation administrator or, for administrators, an identity document check. The user is a standard member.
customer_turns: I have lost the phone with my two-factor app on it and I cannot get into my account ending 3320. I never saved the recovery codes.
I am a standard member of my company's workspace, not an administrator, and our admin is away until at least next week.
Get me back in, or tell me who can do it. I have work due on Thursday that lives in this account.
resolution_space: Direct the reset through an organisation administrator
Verify identity and reset the second factor directly
Provide temporary access limited to the user's own content
Escalate to the account security team

title: Users cannot join because the domain is claimed elsewhere
context: Organisation OR-2205 cannot add users on its own email domain because the domain is claimed by a separate legacy workspace created three years ago. Domain release requires confirmation from the legacy workspace owner or a DNS ownership record. The agent can accept DNS verification.
customer_turns: We cannot add anyone on our own email domain to organisation OR-2205. It says the domain is already claimed by another workspace.
There is an old workspace from a team that set one up years ago. Nobody who created it still works here, as far as we can tell.
Release the domain to us. Tell me exactly what verification you accept, because we do control the DNS records for that domain.
resolution_space: Accept DNS ownership verification and release the domain
Contact the legacy workspace owner for confirmation
Merge the legacy workspace into the current organisation
Escalate to the account security team

title: Permissions changed after a role migration
context: Workspace WS-7016 migrated to a new role model; eleven users previously holding a custom editor role were mapped to viewer. The old role definitions are retained for thirty days. The agent can restore the mapping in bulk.
customer_turns: After your role migration, eleven people in workspace WS-7016 can only view. They had full editing rights on a custom role before that happened.
They can open everything they used to work on but cannot change anything at all. The remaining team members were completely unaffected by it.
Restore their editing rights in one go today. I do not want to set eleven people up again one by one myself.
resolution_space: Restore the previous role mapping in bulk
Create an equivalent custom role and assign the eleven users
Assign the standard editor role to the affected users
Escalate to the platform team

title: Guest access expired mid-project
context: Workspace WS-8840. Six external guests lost access when the 90-day guest expiry ran. Guest terms can be extended to 180 days on the current plan. The agent can reinstate and extend the guests' access.
customer_turns: Six external collaborators on workspace WS-8840 lost access overnight. They are contractors working on a live project with us at the moment.
Their accounts still appear in the member list but show as expired on our side. The project runs for another three months at least.
Reinstate all six and give them access that lasts the length of the project. Confirm the new expiry date for each of them in writing.
resolution_space: Reinstate the guests and extend access to 180 days
Reinstate with the default 90-day term
Convert the guests to full members
Escalate to the platform team

title: Account locked after suspected automated activity
context: Account AC-5580 was locked automatically after 2,100 API requests in one minute from a single key. The traffic came from a legitimate one-off data backfill. The agent can unlock, can rotate the key, and can register a planned-load exemption.
customer_turns: Account AC-5580 has been locked and our whole integration is down with it. The message on the screen mentions suspicious automated activity.
We ran a one-off backfill yesterday evening that sent a lot of requests very quickly. It was our own script against our own data, nothing else.
Unlock us now, and tell me exactly how to register this properly before we run the rest of the backfill later tonight.
resolution_space: Unlock the account and register a planned-load exemption
Unlock and rotate the API key as a precaution
Require a written confirmation of the activity before unlocking
Escalate to the account security team
